full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of the instant petition are that Oli Ahmed, predecessor of respondent Nos.1-8 herein as plaintiff instituted Partition Suit No.270 of 1994 in the 3rd Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong. The plaintiff stated, inter alia, that the suit property belonged to Amin Sharif in 4 annas, Imam Sharif 4 annas, Meherunessa 2 annas and Abdus Sobhan 6 annas share, and accordingly the R.S. Khatian No.1677 was recorded correctly in their names. Abdus Sobhan died leaving behind two sons Sultan Ahmed and Syed Ahmed and daughter Pariya Khatun and they jointly possessed 25 decimals of land of the suit property in their shares according to their family arrangement. Sultan Ahmed and Syed Ahmed sold one gonda of land of Khilla and ditch of R.S. Plot Nos.5570 and 5571 appertaining to R.S. Khatian No.1677 to the original plaintiff Oli Ahmed by registered Kabala dated 16.04.1974 and delivered possession to him. Later on Syed Ahmed sold 41/2 gondas of homestead land of R.S. Plot Nos.5580, 5581 and 5571 by registered Kabala dated 27.07.76 to the original plaintiff Oli Ahmed and delivered possession to him. Thus the original plaintiff became owner of 51/2 gondas of land appertaining to R.S. Khatian No.1677 and he possessed the land by amicable arrangement and accordingly B.S. Khatian has also been recorded jointly in his name along with other co-sharers. Imam Sharif and Meheronnessa died leaving their brother Amin Sharif who thus become owner of 10 decimals of land in the suit property and he possessed the same. Amin Sharif died leaving behind son Abdul Mannan as his heir. As the plaintiff possesses less land than due in his share of 11 decimals of land, he proposed to defendant No.1 for partition of the said share of land as there was no formal partition by metes and bounds. Defendant No.1 refused the request to effect partition of the suit property on 18.01.1991 and hence, the original plaintiff instituted the partition suit claiming a separate saham for his 11 decimals of land. 

 3. Defendant No.1 Sultan Ahmed contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint. He stated, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form; the suit is barred by limitation; the suit is bad for defect of parties and the suit is not properly valued. The further case of defendant No.1 is that the plaintiff has got no possession in the suit property. The P.S. and B.S. Khatians have been recorded in the names of the defendants. Defendant No. 1 and his brother Syed Ahmed sold out 2 decimals of land only to the plaintiff by registered Kabala dated 16.07.1974. Syed Ahmed became insane and left his house and while he was suffering from mental illness he died leaving behind his wife and children. Syed Ahmed did not sell 41/2 gondas, i.e. 9 decimals of land to the original plaintiff while in sound mind and health. If such transfer deed transpires in favour of the plaintiff, it is a collusive fraudulent and ineffective sale. The alleged Kabala dated 27.07.1976 for 9 decimals of land by Syed Ahmed in favour of the plaintiff is false, concocted, without consideration and ineffective one. The heirs of Syed Ahmed are living in the said land. Syed Ahmed has not sold 9 decimals of land to the plaintiff and possession of that land was not delivered. Syed Ahmed has neither executed nor registered the aforesaid kabala for 9 decimals land. This kabala is a forged one created in collusion with the identifier, writer and witnesses by false personification. The plaintiff never possessed any land on the strength of the kabala dated 27.07.1976. The plaintiff's suit is liable to be dismissed.
